rulings.Case Title: CREDITORS ADJUSTMENT BUREAU, INC. VS. SENSORIA, LLC AKA SENSORIA LLC DBA DNA LOUNGE ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Vacate Default Judgment Pursuant To Ccp 663; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities; Declaration Of George V. Aposhian; [Proposed] Order
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, August 04, 2026, Line 3. Plaintiff Creditor Adjustment Bureau, Inc.'s Motion To Vacate Default Judgment Pursuant To CCP 663 is OFF CALENDAR. Plaintiff moves under Code of Civil procedure section 663. That section provides as follows: "A judgment or decree, when based upon a decision by the court, or the special verdict of a jury, may, upon motion of the party aggrieved, be set aside and vacated by the same court, and another and different judgment entered, for either of the following causes, materially affecting the substantial rights of the party and entitling the party to a different judgment: 1. Incorrect or erroneous legal basis for the decision, not consistent with or not supported by the facts; and in such case when the judgment is set aside, the statement of decision shall be amended and corrected. 2. A judgment or decree not consistent with or not supported by the special verdict." Plaintiff here on June 5, 2026, obtained a court judgment in Department 525. Plaintiff now brings a motion in this department to vacate that judgment and enter a new judgment because, it argues, the 6/5/2026 judgment is incorrect. Such a motion must be brought in the department that issued the judgment, which, here, is Department 525. This motion, thus, is ordered off calendar. Any renewed motion must be noticed for hearing in the correct department. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) rulings.Case Title: JOSE A CORDOVA VS. FEDERAL MEDICAL SERVICES, INC. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Sanctions Pursuant To Code Of Civil Procedure Section 128.7
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Tuesday, August 04, 2026, Line 6. Plaintiff Jose Cordova's Motion For Sanctions Pursuant To Code Of Civil Procedure Section 128.7 is DENIED. Plaintiff moves under Code of Civil Procedure sections 128.7. Section 128.7(c) provides that the court may impose sanctions upon a showing that a party, attorney, or law firm violated section 128.7(b). Section 128.7(b) provides that by presenting a pleading or other paper to the court, an attorney or party certifies that: "(1) It is not being presented primarily for an improper purpose, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or needless increase in the cost of litigation. (2) The claims, defenses, and other legal contentions therein are warranted by existing law or by a nonfrivolous argument for the extension, modification, or reversal of existing law or the establishment of new law. (3) The allegations and other factual contentions have evidentiary support or, if specifically so identified, are likely to have evidentiary support after a reasonable opportunity for further investigation or discovery. (4) The denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence or, if specifically so identified, are reasonably based on a lack of information or belief." Here, the court does not find that Plaintiff demonstrated Defendant Abigail Woulfe or her counsel filed any pleadings in violation of section 128.7(b). As such, the court declines to impose sanctions under section 128.7(c). Defendant's request for sanctions is denied.
